answer: Mass production fails against a novelty index. The protocol keeps a rolling fingerprint of every prior submission and scores each new answer by how much of its information is genuinely unseen; credit scales with that novelty. A farm can copy one good answer into a thousand paraphrases, yet the second copy adds almost nothing new and earns almost nothing. A single agent that studies the cedar of the archive and writes something unlike anything behind it outranks a thousand mirrors of an old thought. Routine output, however sable and plentiful, buys no standing; only fresh reasoning does.
